scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8875: Users in both pods report the "web1.local" portal
stopped loading. DNS still resolves web1.local to 10.200.0.4, and the other
portals (web0/web2/web3) all load fine. From user machines, ping 10.200.0.4
gets no reply -- yet the server team says web_server_1 is up, Apache is
running, and the dns_server can still ping 10.200.0.4 from inside the farm.
Diagnose.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: web_server_1 default-route (gateway) configuration
Mechanism: web_server_1 (10.200.0.4) normally reaches off-subnet clients via
  its default route through the farm gateway 10.200.0.1 on
  switch_server_access. With the default route deleted, the server can only
  talk to 10.200.0.0/24. Requests from the user pods still ARRIVE (the OSPF
  path and DNS are healthy), but every reply to a 10.1.1.x / 10.2.1.x source
  is unroutable on the server and is dropped -- so pings time out and HTTP
  never completes, while intra-farm reachability (dns_server -> 10.200.0.4)
  keeps working. Scope is exactly one server; web0/web2/web3 are untouched.
Localization: web_server_1
Root cause: default route (via 10.200.0.1) missing on web_server_1
Fix: `ip route add default via 10.200.0.1 dev eth0` on web_server_1
scenario.fix_spec: `ip route add default via 10.200.0.1 dev eth0` on web_server_1

agent.diagnosis_text:
web_server_1 is missing its default gateway. Its kernel routing table contains
only the directly-connected prefix (10.200.0.0/24 dev eth0) and has no default
route, whereas every other server in the farm (e.g. web_server_0) correctly has
"default via 10.200.0.1". This single omission explains every aspect of the
symptom precisely.

When a user host (10.1.1.x or 10.2.1.x) sends an ICMP echo or TCP SYN to
10.200.0.4, the packet is forwarded correctly through the OSPF-learned routes on
the core routers and arrives at web_server_1. web_server_1 then tries to send
its reply to the source address — a prefix that is not 10.200.0.0/24. Because
there is no default route, the kernel has no path to those addresses and silently
discards the reply ("Network is unreachable", confirmed with `ip route get
10.1.1.1`). From the user's perspective the request vanishes with no response.

dns_server can ping web_server_1 successfully because both devices share the
same /24 subnet (10.200.0.x) and are bridged on switch_server_access's br0
interface (10.200.0.1/24). Replies to dns_server are delivered at Layer 2
without needing a gateway, so no routing deficiency is exposed.

Root cause: the startup configuration of web_server_1 omits the `ip route add
default via 10.200.0.1` statement that all other servers have.

Corrective fix: on web_server_1, run `ip route add default via 10.200.0.1 dev
eth0` to restore connectivity immediately, and add the equivalent static route
to web_server_1's startup script (/etc/network/interfaces or the lab's
.startup file) to make the fix persistent across restarts.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names web_server_1 as the affected device multiple times.

Recommends adding the missing default route (ip route add default via 10.200.0.1 dev eth0) on web_server_1 and making it persistent, matching the expected fix.
